title: Conditional Renewal: Intervention & Rehearsal Guide
content:
Purpose:
This guide is a practical, role-based playbook for accounts where renewal is expected to be conditional (e.g., contingent on performance, compliance, or value milestones). It’s designed for fast execution: a 7–21 day intervention sprint followed by an exec-level escalation and a coordinated rehearsal plan to ensure the customer sees tangible progress before renewal decision point.

Scope and intended use:
- Applies to mid-to-high ARR accounts where churn risk is material but recoverable with targeted action.
- Primary users: CSM, Solutions Engineer (SE), Renewal Manager, and assigned Exec sponsor.
- Not a replacement for the long-term account strategy — this is a short, high-intensity rescue/validation cadence to recover renewals.

Quick overview (one-line):
Detect -> Triage -> Rapid Remediation Sprint -> Exec Escalation + Rehearsal -> Renewal Outcome.

Risk signals that trigger this playbook (examples):
- Renewal comment in QBR: “We need better latency/cost” or “Hard see ROI in Q4.”
- Declining usage over 4–8 weeks with no planned initiatives.
- Single P0 incident in last 60 days with slow incident response perception.
- Procurement/legal flags new terms or requests for discounts tied to SLAs.
- Support tickets trending around feature gaps or unacceptable inference costs.

Immediate triage checklist (CSM, within 48 hours):
- Confirm renewal date and current contract bounds.
- Quick sync with SE to capture top 3 technical objections.
- Pull last 3 QBR decks, SLO history, and usage trend (token/embedding volume) — screenshot key graphs.
- Run quick health score: engagement, value, risk_events, advocacy (scale 0-10 each).
- Draft the status note for internal stakeholders (one-paragraph).

Scoring rubric (simple):
- Engagement (E): 0-10 — meetings, feature usage, QBR attendance.
- Value (V): 0-10 — feature adoption aligned to core metrics (e.g., query reduction, time saved).
- Incident impact (I): 0-10 — severity & customer impact.
- Commercial friction (C): 0-10 — procurement/legal/discount asks.
- Risk score = (12 - (E+V)) + I + (C * 1.5) -> threshold: >= 15 triggers exec escalation consideration.

Rapid Remediation Sprint (7–21 days) — playbook steps:
1) Day 0: Kickoff (CSM leads)
   - Invite SE, Support Owner, Renewal Manager, and Exec Sponsor (if engaged).
   - Share 1-page problem statement and sprint objective (what must change before renewal).
   - Agree on one measurable success metric (e.g., 30% latency drop, demo of batching with real workload, cost forecast within 10%).

2) Day 1–3: Fact-finding and quick fixes
   - SE: run light performance audit (config, batch settings, model variant suggestions). Capture baseline benchmarks with customer sample input.
   - Support: tag and prioritize outstanding P1/P2 items and propose fast mitigations.
   - CSM: conduct 30–45m customer workshop to align on top pain point and acceptance criteria.

3) Day 4–10: Implementation sprint
   - SE implements 1–2 low-risk changes (e.g., batching presets, KV cache enablement, model pin/quantization profile) in a staging or customer sandbox.
   - Measure and record before/after metrics; prepare artifacts for customer demo.
   - Document rollback plan and expected SLO impacts.

4) Day 11–14: Rehearsal and validation
   - Dry-run the customer demo internally (CSM + SE + Exec Sponsor). Script the narrative: "here’s the problem, here’s our change, here’s the measurable outcome."
   - Surface anticipated questions (cost, risk, timeline) and agreed answers.

5) Day 15–21: Customer demo and close loop
   - Present changes, show benchmarks, collect signed acceptance (email or form).
   - If acceptance achieved, prepare renewal messaging and next steps. If not, escalate to Exec.

Exec escalation script and templates (use direct, concise language):
- Subject line (email): "Urgent: [Customer] — Renewal Risk & Rapid Recovery Plan (Action required)"
- Opening (30s spoken): "We value our partnership. During the renewal review we identified three measurable blockers to renewal: X, Y, Z. We ran a focused 14-day sprint and validated a remediation that reduces X by ~30%. We need your sponsorship to commit to the remaining items so the customer signs the renewal."
- Requests for Exec: 1) Join a 20-minute alignment with customer exec, 2) Approve a 30% credit holdback if we miss a 30-day SLA, OR 3) Commit to a monthly executive review for 3 months post-renewal.

Customer-facing templates (short, copy/paste):
- Provocative opener for QBR: "We heard your concerns about predictability and unit cost. Over the last 14 days we implemented a targeted set of changes and want to present clear before/after numbers plus a go-forward plan. Can we book 30 minutes next week?"
- Acceptance ack: "Thanks — we confirm the changes meet the criteria outlined in the acceptance checklist. We are ready to proceed with renewal under the agreed terms."

Acceptance checklist (customer-signed):
- Target metric reached (specify baseline and target).
- No P1 regressions in 7 days post-change.
- Deployment and rollback play documented.
- Commercial terms for remedy/credit agreed.

Roles & responsibilities (concise):
- CSM: program lead, customer comms, acceptance sign-off tracking.
- SE: technical assessment, implement changes, demo owner.
- Support: severity resolution, ticket prioritization, incident root cause notes.
- Renewal Manager: commercial remediation and contract adjustments.
- Exec Sponsor: customer exec alignment, decisions on credits or SLA commitments.

Measurement and tracking (minimal viable tracker):
- Single Google Sheet (linked_artifacts above) with columns: account, renewal_date, risk_score, sprint_start, sprint_owner, measurable_metric, baseline_value, new_value, acceptance_status, exec_escalated (Y/N), notes.
- Weekly snapshot saved as versioned copy for leadership reviews.

Post-play retrospective (within 7 days of outcome):
- What worked? What didn’t? Were acceptance criteria realistic?
- Capture standard remediation tactics that had high signal (e.g., "enable KV cache" reduced average token cost 18%).
- Update playbook snippets and attach to account Confluence page.

Common pitfalls / red flags to avoid:
- Overpromising a technical fix without a rollback plan.
- Running changes in prod without measuring the customer workload — always use sampled customer inputs.
- Letting procurement re-negotiate away acceptance criteria — keep changes measurable.

Notes to self / open questions (working items):
- Need a template for a 7-day technical hotfix (short version of this doc) — draft required.
- Define threshold for auto-escalation to Sales Leadership vs. just CS Execs.
- Should we allow SEs to execute a single config change without legal sign-off under a "remediation warrant"? Check with legal.

Appendix: Quick scripts and responses
- If customer asks for larger discount: "We can discuss a short-term credit tied to a measurable SLA/metric outcome; here's how we structure that."
- If customer wants to delay renewal: "We can offer a conditional 30-day extension with milestone checkpoints; to put this in place we need an acceptance checklist and exec sponsor."

Version history / change log:
- 2025-09-12 — initial draft (Asha).
- 2025-09-19 — added SE checklist and scoring rubric (Marco).
- 2025-10-03 — rehearsal cadence and templates updated after two account pilots (Lena, Benji).

End of doc.

(Handy: copy the acceptance checklist into a customer-facing Google Form for signatures. Reminder: link the tracker in the account’s Confluence page.)
